subject.title: Feature: Floating agent bubbles (Clawi) for macOS

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor persistent per-agent floating windows as a first-party macOS companion feature, or first create a native UI/window extension boundary for an external implementation?
rationale: The feature introduces a new persistent desktop interaction, accessibility model, state owner, and agent/session routing concept that source-level implementation choices cannot safely settle without product intent.

options.title: Sponsor native bubbles
options.body: Define and implement the feature inside the macOS companion using canonical activity and WebChat routing surfaces.

options.title: Design an extension boundary
options.body: First expose a reviewed native window and session-routing API so an external app or plugin can own the optional visual experience.

options.title: Decline the interaction
options.body: Close the request if persistent floating agent windows do not fit the intended macOS companion experience.

recommendation.title: Sponsor native bubbles
recommendation.body: Define and implement the feature inside the macOS companion using canonical activity and WebChat routing surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the documented project maintainer, were explicitly asked for direction, and already supplied the issue's keep-open product assessment.
